6	
7	## How to use this
8	
9	- The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo.

12	
13	## Theme palette
14	
15	A cool indigo-biased neutral set with an amber-gold action colour and a permanently-dark navigation rail. Apply these to the existing spartan CSS tokens in `src/styles.css` (the `:root` and `:root.dark` blocks). Names below are roles; map each to spartan's own token (for example the action colour is spartan's `--primary`, the subtle hover background is spartan's `--accent`, which is a different thing; do not confuse the two).
16	
17	```
18	role                     light        dark
19	----                     -----        ----
20	action / primary         #d8891a      #f5b843
21	on-primary               #ffffff      #241a05
22	page background          #f6f7fa      #0e1018
23	foreground (text)        #1b1e2b      #eceef6
24	card / popover           #ffffff      #171a26
25	muted surface            #eef0f6      #1e2231
26	muted foreground         #5b6072      #9aa0b4
27	border / input           #e4e7ef      #272b3b
28	focus ring               amber @ 35%  amber @ 40%
29	--- navigation rail (dark in both themes) ---
30	sidebar background       #1e2233      #10121c
31	sidebar foreground       #eceef6      #eceef6
32	sidebar muted            #9aa0b4      #8b90a6
33	sidebar active bg        #2a2f45      #20263c
34	--- semantic (separate from the accent; these carry meaning) ---
35	success (Active)         #2fb574      #3ecb84
36	warning (Injured)        #e4802b      #f0983f
37	destructive (MIA/retire) #e5484d      #f2585d
38	info                     #4f7cf0      #6f97f6
39	```
40	
41	Radius: cards and controls around 9-10px, dialogs a touch larger. Elevation is restrained: one soft shadow on cards, a stronger one only on popovers and dialogs. Do not stamp the same shadow and radius on every block.
42	
43	Theme switch is a `.dark` class toggled on `<html>` (the substrate already defines `:root` and `:root.dark`). Persist the choice; respect `prefers-color-scheme` when the user has made no choice.

45	## Icon scheme
46

49	```
50	usage                 lucide icon
51	-----                 -----------
52	nav: Dashboard        lucideLayoutDashboard
53	nav: Roster           lucideUsers
54	nav: Missions         lucideTarget   (or lucideRadar)
55	nav: Threats          lucideShieldAlert
56	nav: Recruit          lucideUserPlus
57	nav: Settings         lucideSettings
58	theme light / dark    lucideSun / lucideMoon
59	search                lucideSearch
60	notifications         lucideBell
61	edit                  lucidePencil
62	retire / delete       lucideTrash2
63	deploy                lucideCrosshair
64	back                  lucideChevronLeft
65	select chevron        lucideChevronDown
66	stat: heroes          lucideUserCheck
67	stat: missions live   lucideActivity
68	stat: avg power       lucideZap
69	stat: threats         lucideShieldAlert
70	success / warning     lucideCheck / lucideTriangleAlert
71	```

73	## Low-fidelity layout
74	
75	Structure and regions, not styling. Each note says what happens at 375px.
76	
77	App shell (all screens):
78	
79	```
80	+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
81	| RAIL   |  TOPBAR: [menu] crumbs .... [search][bell][thm][av] |
82	| (dark) +-------------------------------------------------+
83	| brand  |                                                 |
84	| ------ |   ROUTED SCREEN CONTENT (scrolls)               |
85	| nav x6 |                                                 |
86	| ------ |                                                 |
87	| user   |                                                 |
88	+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
89	375px: rail becomes an off-canvas drawer (hlm-sidebar handles this).
90	       CLOSED drawer must be display:none or aria-hidden, NOT just
91	       translated off-screen, or the responsive gate flags it as an
92	       element escaping the viewport. Topbar search collapses to an
93	       icon that expands, or drops below the crumbs.
94	```
95	
96	Dashboard:
97	
98	```
99	[ Operations Dashboard ]                        [ + Recruit ]
100	[ stat ][ stat ][ stat ][ stat ]      <- grid, auto-fit min ~210px
101	[ Top heroes this cycle ]             [ View all roster ]
102	[ hero ][ hero ][ hero ][ hero ]      <- grid, auto-fill min ~230px
103	[ Roster ]                            [ 42 heroes ]
104	[ ============ ROSTER TABLE ============ ]
105	375px: stat tiles -> 1 per row; hero cards -> 1-2 per row; table below.
106	```
107	
108	Roster table:
109	
110	```
111	+--------------------------------------------------------------+
112	| [search........]  [class v]                    [ + Recruit ] |
113	+--------------------------------------------------------------+
114	| HERO            | CLASS  | POWER | STATUS   | CLEAR | ACTIONS |
115	| (av) Name/ID    | badge  |  88   | pill     | Tier4 | edit del|
116	| ...                                                          |
117	+--------------------------------------------------------------+
118	| 42 of 42 heroes                          sorted by power     |
119	+--------------------------------------------------------------+
120	375px: a plain table WILL overflow. Two allowed answers, pick one and
121	       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto
122	       container so the CONTAINER scrolls and the page does not (the
123	       gate exempts intentional scroll containers); or (b) switch to a
124	       stacked card list below ~640px (each hero a card). (b) is the
125	       nicer result; (a) is the cheaper one. Do NOT let the page itself
126	       scroll sideways.
127	```
128	
129	Hero detail:
130	
131	```
132	[< Back to roster]
133	[ (AV lg) ID / Name / Alias / badges ]            [Deploy][Retire]
134	[ Overview | Powers | Missions | Edit ]           <- tabs
135	Overview:  [ Field summary + 3 mini-stats ]  [ Dossier k/v ]
136	Powers:    [ power meters ]                   [ ability badges ]
137	Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
138	Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),
139	             notes(textarea), active(switch) ; Cancel / Save ]
140	           Retire -> confirmation dialog.
141	375px: two-column areas stack to one column; form grid -> 1 column;
142	       tab strip scrolls horizontally if needed; detail header wraps.
143	```
144	
145	## Build guidelines
146	
147	Component map (region -> spartan primitive):
148	
149	- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
150	- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
151	- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
152	- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
153	- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
154	- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.
155	
156	MVVM (the house pattern, enforced):
157	
158	- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.
159	- The component lists its VM in its own `providers: [XViewModel]` (component-scoped, NOT `providedIn: 'root'`), injects it, and binds the template to `vm` signals. The component class stays thin: no business logic, no `.subscribe`, state lives in the VM.
160	- Presentational pieces (hero card, stat tile, power meter) live under `src/app/ui/`, take `input()`/`output()`, inject no data service.
161	- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.
162	
163	Responsive rules (the build MUST satisfy the Part 5 gate at 375 / 768 / 1280):
164	
165	- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.
166	- Any wide block (the table) either scrolls inside its own `overflow-x:auto` container or restructures (cards) below a breakpoint. The page body never scrolls sideways.
167	- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
168	- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.
169	
170	Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.
171	
172	## The off-canvas gate refinement (constitution to-do)
173	
174	Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.
175	
176	## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)
177	
178	Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Mark it plainly as example data. The specifics (threat tiers, power classes, clearance) are the detail that makes this a real console rather than a generic CRUD table.

1 --- 2 name: house-style 3 description: The house frontend conventions for this repo, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs. Read before writing or editing any component. Covers BEM markup with Tailwind applied in the component stylesheet, the three-file component, the layout grammar (grid for regions, flex for inline runs, no nested flex faking a grid) and the no-raw-literals rule for hand-written CSS. Where these rules and the spartan docs' examples disagree about where utility classes go, these rules win. 4 --- 5 6 # House frontend conventions 7 8 These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. 9 10 ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet 11 12 A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 13 14 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 15 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 16 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 17 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 18 5. **Utilities live in `@apply`, and every rule below still applies to them.** Semantic color tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions, appearance never on a primitive. Moving a utility from the template into `@apply` does not change whether it is allowed. 19 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. 20 21 Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. 22 23 ```html 24 25

The hero detail screen is built. `ng build` exits 0, `npm run lint` is clean, and the two unit tests pass.

**What's there**
- **Route and data:** `detail/:id` reads the id through `toSignal` and loads the hero from `HeroService`. An unknown id shows a "Hero not found" state.
- **Header:** back link, avatar, ID, name, alias, and badges for class, status and clearance tier. Deploy (disabled unless the hero is Active) and Retire.
- **Tabs:** Overview (three stat tiles and dossier), Powers (power meters and ability badges), Missions (deployment log with result badges), and Edit.
- **Edit:** a signal form built from the zod schema, submitted through `FormRoot` and `submission.action`. Save and Cancel are in the template; Cancel discards edits and returns to Overview.
- **Retire:** goes through an `hlm-dialog`. Confirming removes the hero and returns to the roster; the dialog is closed by its template reference.
- **Icons:** registered per component with `provideIcons`, using the scheme's names.

**Decisions to check**
- **Retire** removes the hero from the roster. The model has no "retired" status, so I didn't add one.
- **Active switch** moves a hero between Active and Reserve. Injured and MIA heroes keep their status unless the switch is flipped.
- **Domain additions:** `notes` on each hero, a mission log, `deploy()` and `retire()` on the store, and `POWER_ABILITIES`. All of this is example data.
- **Ability levels** are estimated from the power index. The screen labels them that way.
- **`formMeta`** now returns a keyed type instead of a string index signature, so the template reads field labels type-safely. Its only other caller is the edit schema.

**Not verified**
- I didn't run the browser gates (`check:boot`, `check:interaction`, `check:responsive`, `check:contrast`). The dialog, tabs and 375px layout are unverified beyond the build.

- Budget warnings, not errors: the initial bundle is about 97 kB over its 500 kB budget, and `hero-detail.css` is 2.5 kB over its 4 kB component budget. `heroes.css` is also over, so this predates my change.
